microtheory.name: pragmatics_linguistics
microtheory.definition: Language in context. Speaker meaning vs sentence meaning. Grice's cooperative principle, speech act theory (Austin, Searle), deixis, relevance theory (Sperber + Wilson), politeness (Brown + Levinson). What makes the same sentence mean different things in different contexts. Substrate analogue: substrate's context-conditioned interpretation of incoming messages + drive-conditioned production.

concepts.name: speaker_meaning
concepts.definition: What the speaker intends to communicate, which may differ from literal sentence meaning. Grice. Substrate analogue: substrate's intention attribute on Message.

concepts.name: literal_meaning
concepts.definition: What sentence means independent of speaker intent. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional Concept derivation from Message.

concepts.name: contextualism
concepts.definition: Meaning irreducibly depends on context. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-Mt interpretation framework.

concepts.name: cooperative_principle
concepts.definition: Grice 1975. 'Make your contribution as required by the accepted purpose of the talk exchange.' Substrate analogue: substrate's dialogue-coordination drive.

concepts.name: maxim_of_quantity
concepts.definition: Be as informative as required; not more. Substrate analogue: substrate's parsimony drive in communication.

concepts.name: maxim_of_quality
concepts.definition: Don't say what you believe false; don't say what you lack evidence for. Substrate analogue: substrate's coherence drive in communication.

concepts.name: maxim_of_relation
concepts.definition: Be relevant. Substrate analogue: substrate's relevance computation against current Mt context.

concepts.name: maxim_of_manner
concepts.definition: Be perspicuous: clear, brief, orderly, unambiguous. Substrate analogue: substrate's communication clarity drive.

concepts.name: conversational_implicature
concepts.definition: Inferred from maxim apparent-flouting. 'Some students passed' → not all (Quantity). 'John is a fine friend' said of betrayer → sarcasm (Quality flout). Substrate analogue: substrate's contextual default-inference.

concepts.name: speech_act
concepts.definition: Austin 1962, Searle 1969. Saying = doing. Asserting, asking, commanding, promising, declaring. Substrate analogue: substrate's Message-as-action.

concepts.name: locutionary_act
concepts.definition: Act of saying (the utterance itself). Substrate analogue: substrate's Message production.

concepts.name: illocutionary_act
concepts.definition: Act IN saying. Force: asserting / asking / commanding. Substrate analogue: substrate's Message intention attribute.

concepts.name: perlocutionary_act
concepts.definition: Effect BY saying. Convincing, persuading, frightening. Substrate analogue: substrate's downstream-effect from Message.

concepts.name: felicity_conditions
concepts.definition: Conditions for speech act to succeed. 'I pronounce you married' requires authorized speaker + valid couple. Substrate analogue: substrate's speech-act precondition check.

concepts.name: indirect_speech_act
concepts.definition: Speech act performed by uttering different speech act type. 'Can you pass the salt?' is request, not question. Substrate analogue: substrate's intent-recognition over literal form.

concepts.name: performative_utterance
concepts.definition: Utterance that performs the act named. 'I promise', 'I declare', 'I bet'. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-effecting Message.

concepts.name: deixis
concepts.definition: Reference dependent on context of utterance. Person (I, you), place (here, there), time (now, then). Substrate analogue: substrate's context-bound reference.

concepts.name: anaphora
concepts.definition: Pronoun resolution from previous context. 'John arrived. He waved.' Substrate analogue: substrate's reference-resolution mechanism.

concepts.name: cataphora
concepts.definition: Pronoun precedes referent. 'When she arrived, Mary was hungry.' Substrate analogue: substrate's forward-reference resolution.

concepts.name: relevance_theory
concepts.definition: Sperber + Wilson 1986. One cognitive principle: maximize cognitive effects, minimize processing effort. Replaces Gricean maxims. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive_parsimony in communication interpretation.

concepts.name: common_ground
concepts.definition: Stalnaker. Mutual knowledge between conversation participants. Updates with each utterance. Substrate analogue: substrate's shared-context tracker between Mts.

concepts.name: given_new
concepts.definition: Information already in common ground (given) vs new. Affects intonation + word order. Substrate analogue: substrate's known-vs-novel concept distinction.

concepts.name: politeness_theory
concepts.definition: Brown + Levinson 1987. Face threats (acts that risk hearer's self-image). Mitigation strategies: positive politeness (camaraderie), negative politeness (deference), indirectness, hints. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity-protection across communicators.

concepts.name: positive_face
concepts.definition: Desire to be appreciated + included. Substrate analogue: substrate's relatedness drive.

concepts.name: negative_face
concepts.definition: Desire for autonomy + freedom from imposition. Substrate analogue: substrate's autonomy drive.

concepts.name: honorifics
concepts.definition: Grammaticalized politeness. Japanese -san/-sama, Korean speech levels. Substrate analogue: substrate's politeness-conditioned form selection.

concepts.name: conversation_analysis
concepts.definition: Sacks + Schegloff + Jefferson 1974. Turn-taking, adjacency pairs (question-answer, greeting-greeting), repair. Substrate analogue: substrate's dialogue structure.

concepts.name: turn_taking
concepts.definition: Conversation organized around speakership transitions. Substrate analogue: substrate's communicative-role exchange.

concepts.name: adjacency_pair
concepts.definition: Two-utterance sequences where first creates expectation for specific second. Question-answer, summons-response. Substrate analogue: substrate's dialogue-step pairing.

concepts.name: repair
concepts.definition: Mechanisms for handling problems in talk. Self-repair, other-repair. 'I mean...', 'You said...?' Substrate analogue: substrate's error-correction in dialogue.

rules.name: gricean_inference_from_maxim_violation
rules.head: the substrate notices an utterance apparently flouting a maxim
rules.body: it infers what the speaker intends — sarcasm (Quality flout), over-informativeness implicature (Quantity flout). Substrate's cooperative-inference.

rules.name: speech_act_recognition_drives_response
rules.head: the substrate receives a Message
rules.body: it identifies the illocutionary force (request, assertion, question), and that force determines the response type. Substrate's intent-attribute drives response.

rules.name: indirect_speech_acts_require_pragmatic_recognition
rules.head: the substrate receives a literally-questioning utterance in a context where action is expected
rules.body: it recognises an indirect request + responds appropriately. Substrate's pragmatic intent-recognition.

rules.name: deixis_requires_context_to_resolve
rules.head: the substrate processes a deictic expression
rules.body: it must consult context (speaker, time, place) to compute reference. Substrate's contextual reference-resolution.

rules.name: politeness_modulates_form_for_face_threats
rules.head: the substrate produces an utterance that could threaten the hearer's face
rules.body: it applies politeness mitigation: indirection, hedging, distance markers. Substrate's identity-respecting form selection.
